newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Haider toasts decade as far-right head.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Haider toasts decade as far-right head.

text.p: Austrian far right leader Joerg Haider on Sunday celebrated his 10th anniversary at the head of the Freedom Party after telling 2,000 cheering supporters his first decade in office had just been a warm-up.
"This was just the warm up training. Now we'll really get started," Haider told the crowd of party faithfuls gathered in the southern Austrian town of Klagenfurt on Saturday.
Since his election to party leader in 1986, Haider has transformed the Freedom Party from a fringe group with little support into Europe's biggest far-right parliamentary grouping.

Haider's strong anti-immigration, law-and-order rhetoric has struck a chord with many voters weary of the established coalition government of Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party. But it has brought him few friends outside his own political following.

In 1991, Haider had to resign as provinical governor of Carinthia after praising Adolf Hitler's labour policies and in 1995 he had to backtrack after referring to Nazi extermination camps as "punishment camps".
But 46-year-old Haider, who prefers to dress casually and sports a tan almost year-round, said he had no regrets.
"I have been called a far-right extremist, a fascist and a neo-nazi. But all I wanted was to create a more human society in Austria," he told his supporters.
"I have never cared about ideology, only about basic values such as faith, honour and family."
Haider stood by his goal to steer the Freedom Party to victory in Austria's 1999 general elections and to replace Social Democrat Franz Vranitzky as chancellor.
"This will come automatically. I stand by my plans to become chancellor in 1998," he told Reuters after his speech.
Recent voter surveys have given the party 25 percent support, up from 22 percent in last December's general elections and just a few points behind the People's Party.

Haider's anniversary bash came as Austria's political parties gear up for the country's first European Parliament elections on October 13 and Vienna city hall elections on the same day. Austria joined the European Union last year.
